answer: Use proof-of-unique-human-time via a delayed sequential puzzle. At registration, each key must compute a memory-hard, non-parallel hash chain seeded by its public key and the previous block, taking exactly seven days on one core. The verifier checks a short checkpoint trail in seconds. A gale of new keys cannot shortcut it, since every chain is sequential and each vertex of the trail depends on the last. Fakes need one dedicated core and RAM, so an oasis of cheap clones costs about eight dollars per identity.
